Subject: Accelerator cohort — credits question

Hi Laura,

Quick question as we prep for the LaunchScale cohort kickoff: our startups get a package from the accelerator (cloud credits + partner promos). A few founders asked whether Redwood’s startup credits and the LaunchScale partner promo can be combined for the same trial period, or if there are any stacking limits we should communicate.

A couple of constraints to flag on our side: the cohort promo is 3 months, distributed as a one-time allocation. Founders are US-based, and we generally prefer to have credits applied to the sponsor (us) and then allocated to teams to avoid billing surprises.

Can you outline Redwood’s policy for:
- stacking external accelerator promos with Redwood startup credits
- any per-account caps or expiration alignment we need to know
- who's the right contact to run a batch allocation if we get approvals

Appreciate a quick note — cohort starts Feb 1.

Thanks,
Ethan
LaunchScale Labs

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Accelerator cohort — credits question

Ethan — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: we can usually support stacking partner/cohort promos with a Redwood starter credit, but there are a few operational and policy checks to run first. High level:

- Stacking: Allowed in most cases, provided the promos are applied at different allocation levels (e.g., Redwood credit on the org billing account + cohort promo applied as a sub-account allocation).
- Caps: We enforce a per-customer credit cap for promotional stacking to prevent unlimited compounding; standard cap for accelerator deals is $40k total promotional credit per startup for the first 90 days unless an exception is approved.
- Expiry alignment: If the cohort promo uses a different expiry window, we can mirror that on the Redwood allocation by issuing a custom grant.
- Batch allocation contact: our Programs Ops team handles bulk actions — copying in Karthik here to coordinate allocation workflow and any paperwork.

Can you send a short list of sample founders (3–5) with expected usage patterns (token estimates or expected calls/month)? That will let us size the grant and confirm the stacking is safe for each account. If you want, we can also issue a conditional offer letter that lists the stacking terms.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Growth Lead, Partner Programs
Redwood Inference

Ethan — adding operational detail from the Dedicated/Allocations side. A few specifics that will matter for LaunchScale’s workflow:

1) Deal & allocation model
   - We create a sponsor org in Redwood and then attach sub-accounts for each startup. Sponsor (LaunchScale) can pre-fund the sponsor org or we can issue conditional grants that auto-apply when a startup signs up.

2) Stacking rules (system constraints)
   - System will not allow two simultaneous org-level credits to apply to the same invoice line. To stack, we either:
     a) apply Redwood credit at the org-level and cohort promo as a manual sub-account allocation, or
     b) grant both as sub-account allocations that the sponsor controls.

3) Caps & exceptions
   - Default cap: $40,000 equivalent promotional credit per startup within 90 days.
   - Exceptions: program-level exceptions require a short BU approval (email) + executive signoff for anything above $75k.

4) Timing & batch process
   - For cohort start Feb 1, we need a founder list and token estimate by Jan 20 to have allocations live the week of Jan 25.

I’ll stand up a sandbox allocation for a pilot of 10 accounts if you want to test the UX.

-Karthik
Head of RevOps, Redwood Inference
